description: Commands the shell tool may run, each with a short note for the model.
A command that also exists as its own tool (tools/<name>/tool.json)
is refused by the shell: the dedicated tool wins.
A command not installed on the machine is left out of help and refused.
"needs": "x" means the command runs the folder's own code (make runs the Makefile),
so it needs execute access where it runs.
Every command runs in a sandbox that sees only the folders in context/paths.json,
environment adds to each command's environment: path lists folders searched before
/usr/bin, as the sandbox sees them (under /usr, or /work/<name>/... with x access);
variables are exported, ${NAME} taking NAME from the tool's own environment
(the agents set AGENT_NAME). The sandbox's own variables (PATH, HOME, GIT_*, ...)
refused: commands a model often tries that are not available, each with the reason and what
to do instead, which the refusal says.

refused.curl: the shell has no network; read web pages with the web tool
refused.wget: the shell has no network; read web pages with the web tool
refused.python: there is no Python or other script interpreter; use the shell's commands, or ask the user
refused.python3: there is no Python or other script interpreter; use the shell's commands, or ask the user
refused.pip: there is no Python or other script interpreter; use the shell's commands, or ask the user
refused.perl: there is no Python or other script interpreter; use the shell's commands, or ask the user
refused.node: there is no Python or other script interpreter; use the shell's commands, or ask the user
refused.ruby: there is no Python or other script interpreter; use the shell's commands, or ask the user
refused.sudo: commands run as the user, in a sandbox, without sudo

commands.ar: list or extract static libraries (ar t lib.a)
commands.basename: strip the folder from a path
commands.chmod: change permissions (chmod +x script.sh; running it still needs x access)
commands.clang-format: format C/C++ source (clang-format -i src/x.c edits in place); the style is the project's .clang-format, else the agents' template
commands.clang-tidy: find bugs and style problems in C/C++ (clang-tidy file.c -- -Isrc/include)

cmake.about: configure and build with the project's CMakeLists.txt (runs the project's build logic)

commands.ctags: index the symbols of source files
commands.date: print the date and time; TZ=Asia/Tokyo date for another time zone, date -u for UTC
commands.df: free space on the file system
commands.dirname: strip the file name from a path
commands.du: disk space used by files and folders
commands.find: find files by name, type, size or date

gdb.about: debug a program, e.g. gdb -batch -ex run -ex bt ./prog (runs the program)

commands.git: git, read-only: status, log, show, diff, blame, grep, ls-files, restore (undo edits), listing branches and tags. The pr tool commits and opens pull requests; pr with action sync updates from GitHub
commands.head: first lines of a file
commands.join: join lines on a common field

make.about: build with the folder's Makefile; to add flags and keep the Makefile's, set them before it: CPPFLAGS='-DNAME=1' CFLAGS='-Wno-unused-parameter' make (make CFLAGS=... replaces the Makefile's flags)

commands.mktemp: create a temporary file or folder (mktemp -d)

ninja.about: build with the folder's build.ninja, e.g. cmake -G Ninja -B build, then cd build && ninja (runs the project's build rules)

commands.od: dump a file in octal or hex
commands.pkg-config: compiler and linker flags for installed libraries
commands.readlink: show where a link points (readlink -f resolves it fully)
commands.rg: ripgrep: fast recursive search (rg -n pattern src; -t c for C files only, -l lists files, -w whole words)
commands.sed: stream editor (sed -n '10,20p' prints lines; sed -i edits in place)
commands.shellcheck: check shell scripts for bugs (shellcheck script.sh)
commands.shfmt: format shell scripts (shfmt -d -i 4 script.sh shows the changes; -w writes them)
commands.size: section sizes of an object file
commands.tar: create, list or extract archives (tar -czf, -tzf, -xzf), inside the allowed folders
commands.tee: copy input to a file and to the output
commands.touch: create files or update their dates
commands.truncate: shrink or extend a file to a size
commands.uname: print the system's name, kernel and architecture (uname -a for all)
commands.xxd: dump a file in hex, e.g. xxd -s 64 -l 32 file (-r turns a dump back into bytes)
